text:
maria: quick follow-up on the prefix cache RFC from yesterday. two things still bugging me: 1) staleness vs memory cost for long-lived prefixes (per-tenant segmentation blows up memory), and 2) the lease handoff race we hit in the load tests. proposing: add a per-tenant soft_ttl (staleness window) + a global eviction-priority queue that accepts affinity hints. also add a lightweight Pin API to lock a prefix for short lived sessions. thoughts?
josh: +1 on soft_ttl, we have telemetry that shows a small fraction of tenants cause most churn. example from last test: 
```
OOM @ node-12 2026-02-11T19:23:12Z
eviction loop: tenant=tenant-A prefixes_evicted=3245 reclaim=1.2GB
````
we could make soft_ttl adaptive by observing reaccess rate.
neha: hierarchical cache is worth considering: per-worker slab for hot prefixes + a shared fallback pool. pros: limits noisy-tenant blast radius. cons: complexity for lease migration and accounting. if we do this, we should ship behind a feature flag and a migration shim that rehomes prefixes lazily.
samir: correctness note: any solution that moves ownership needs read-after-write guarantees. the lease handoff must be linearizable wrt prefix inserts/evicts. current proto uses a best-effort revoke which caused the race. propose extending the lease handshake with a short two-phase commit: owner->candidate prepare(seq), candidate becomes active on commit(seq), owner releases only after commit ack or after timeout with tombstone. seq is monotonic per-prefix.
maria: that two-phase commit seems heavier but safe. what perf hit are we talking about?
josh: put numbers: prepare/commit adds ~200-400us on the critical path in our bench with colocated nodes. we can amortize by batching prepares for multi-prefix handoffs.
karen: rollout plan question: we need a clear migration path from current per-prefix single-owner model to something that supports soft_ttl + shared pool. suggests a 3-step plan: 1) telemetry + soft_ttl defaults (no ownership changes), 2) opt-in hierarchical shared pool + feature flag, 3) full lease handoff with two-phase commit and deprecation of old revoke path. each step gated by canary and qps/latency checks.
runtime-bot: load-test-operator: alert: second run showed lease-revoke latency spike 2.4x at t=19:25, tied to tenant-A churn.
infra-bot: deploy: pushed cache-metrics-update -> staging (build b-2026.02.12-07).
samir: also callout: metrics we need now: per-prefix last-write-seq, last-lease-acquire-ts, reaccess-count(window=5m), evict-retry-count. without those it's hard to tune soft_ttl.
neha: agree. also: eviction priority queue should accept a stable affinity token so hot prefixes for a tenant can be assigned lower eviction priority. that gives predictable QoS for paying customers.
maria: action items: (1) josh/infra add the metrics above (2) neha spike hierarchical slab + feature flag (3) samir prototype two-phase handoff sketch + perf microbench (4) karen draft rollout checklist and canary thresholds. i'll draft a short RFC amendment with these items. thanks all :thumbsup:
